assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 as an incretin and its translation into durable agonists is a rare case in which basic endocrine physiology produced therapies that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit now documented in large outcome trials. Originality and clarity of the physiological mechanism are high and the societal impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Holst established the physiology of GLP-1 and its insulinotropic role, Drucker defined the proglucagon-derived peptide biology and the therapeutic rationale, and Mojsov identified the biologically active truncated peptide GLP-1(7-36). Habener's contribution is not on the credited list, and Knudsen's role is industrial drug development. The three-name set is plausible but the credit between academic discovery and drug development is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently over decades, with multiple approved drugs and large randomized outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably urgent.
uncertainties: Relative weight of Mojsov versus Habener (not in the credited names) and of Knudsen's industrial peptide engineering is disputed.
I am relying on my own recollection of the primary-discovery chronology rather than independent verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and have opened a new therapeutic modality, with growing extension to autoimmunity. The conceptual and clinical impact is large and clearly defined.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed the costimulatory CAR design and preclinical proof, June led the first successful clinical trials of CD19 CAR-T, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Zelig Eshhar, originator of the chimeric receptor concept, is not among the credited names and I will not add him; this leaves a real gap in a fair allocation.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and years of follow-up confirm durable responses; limitations in solid tumours and toxicity remain, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: The credited names omit the original chimeric receptor concept, which may make any three-person set unfair.
Rosenberg's contribution is partly to the broader cell-therapy field rather than CAR-T specifically.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with light, and has become a routine tool across many fields. It is an invention of lasting methodological importance, with early therapeutic steps in vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification and characterization by Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) was the decisive molecular discovery; Boyden and Deisseroth demonstrated neuronal control, with Deisseroth also developing the broader toolkit and applications; Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted approach is also credited. With six names for three slots, the allocation is difficult and contested. I select the two channelrhodopsin discoverers plus Deisseroth as the most defensible balance.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used for over fifteen years; recognition is timely, though clinical translation is still early.
uncertainties: Allocation among Boyden, Deisseroth, Bamberg, Miesenböck, Nagel and Hegemann is genuinely unresolved.
The prize category question, tool development versus mechanism, is arguable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling logic from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus and underlies understanding of proteostasis, secretory-cell function and disease including diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The discovery is conceptually clean and original.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily delineated the Ire1/Hac1 (XBP1) pathway and the signalling mechanism, with Walter extending to the mechanism of Ire1 activation and later regulation of translation. The two-person set is clear and well supported.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed and conserved across eukaryotes; the basic mechanism is stable and recognition is timely, with therapeutic modulation of the pathway still under development.
uncertainties: Contributions of other pioneers of ER stress signalling, such as Kozutsumi or Ron, are not in the credited names and I cannot weigh them from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted inhibition of the BCR-ABL kinase turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and proved the principle of oncogene-directed therapy. Impact and clarity are very high.
assessment.attribution: Lydon and Druker drove the development of imatinib and its clinical translation, and Sawyers contributed the resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors. The chemistry origins at Ciba-Geigy/Novartis and earlier discoverers of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion are partly outside the credited names, which complicates the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of long-term survival data and independent confirmation make this fully mature. Its fame may make it feel less novel but it is fully mature.
uncertainties: Medicine-side recognition of this area has partly occurred through earlier awards, and the overlap with the cancer-driver discoveries upstream is unclear.
Credit for the original chemistry is not captured in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides for SMN2 yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy and a template for RNA-targeted drugs. The link from an RNA-processing mechanism to a clinical outcome is direct and clear. I judge this through scientific criteria; my field expertise should not by itself raise the ranking.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the SMN2 exon 7 splicing regulation and the antisense strategy, and Bennett developed the oligonucleotide chemistry and the drug. Others such as Hua and Kole contributed to early antisense splice modulation and are not credited. The two-person set is coherent but incomplete in the broader history.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term data and independent follow-up; recognition would be reasonably timely, though the effects of long-term treatment are still being characterized.
uncertainties: Credit for earlier antisense splice-correction concepts may be undervalued in the credited names.
Magnitude of benefit varies by treatment timing and disease type.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cell survival, not only proliferation, drives cancer, defined the mitochondrial apoptosis pathway regulation and enabled BH3-mimetic therapy with venetoclax. The significance is large and the mechanistic story is coherent.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the discovery and functional dissection of the BCL-2 family, and Vaux demonstrated the oncogenic cooperation and survival function. Strasser is an important later contributor. Credit from other laboratories, such as the t(14;18) cloning work and early BCL-2 function studies, is not among the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mature with an approved drug class and consistent confirmation; recognition is reasonably timely, though apoptosis was already honoured in 2002.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 apoptosis prize may reduce its priority.
Priority for the original BCL-2 cloning in different laboratories is not captured by the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chaperonin-assisted folding established that proteins fold inside defined cellular machines, with consequences for protein misfolding disease and cellular proteostasis. The discovery is original and fundamental, with a clear mechanistic account.
assessment.attribution: Horwich and Hartl jointly demonstrated the function of the GroEL/GroES and mitochondrial Hsp60 system in assisted folding in vivo and in vitro, making a clean two-person allocation. Contributions from earlier chaperone work, such as Ellis, are not on the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Long established and independently confirmed; some might say timely recognition has been delayed, though the discovery remains of ongoing relevance.
uncertainties: Direct medical impact is more indirect than in several other candidates.
Earlier chaperone concepts are not captured in the credited names.
